interpretation: Positive source-backed co-geography between modelled local WW production and relative GBIF-indexed introduced candidate butterfly larval host richness persists after country, coarse geography, indexed host count, 2021 built and crop, and WWTP count controls.
An independent WWTP number coefficient no longer differs reliably from zero after these controls; baseline global WWTP association remains an observational result.
Small model R2 increment of adding production to WWTP+urban+crop does not establish a meaningful out-of-sample forecast improvement or a causal nutrient process.
Modeled untreated wastewater and modeled treatment share provide no robust evidence of sewage nutrient enrichment when the full urban+WWTP+production controls are included.
limits: 2015 modeled wastewater generation and treatment volumes are NOT observed nitrogen loads or discharge to terrestrial plants.
2015 PANGAEA 5 arcmin gridded values, 2019 WPI, 2021 WorldCover and pooled 2001–2024 GBIF records are not synchronous exposures.
500m city-cover sampling, 25km WW production, 25km WWTP count and 5km botanical observations differ in footprint.
2015 modelled wastewater grids derive from human return flows, so residual associations may reflect human settlement/industry and plant sampling rather than sewage enrichment.
Contemporary nonnative candidate host regions do not establish plant introduction on individual ports or butterfly colonization.
Data selected to 42 eligible countries and 1055 ports; missing global coast satellite pixels and biased WWTP country coverage constrain generality.
Island host-butterfly distribution and original GEB +54.9% remain separate ecological outcomes, no full causal chain shown.
